title: Serving 2 Million Models Without Melting: Scaling the Hugging Face Hub — Arek Borucki, Hugging Face
talk_summary: A Hugging Face platform engineer describes how the Hub scaled search and metadata to 3M models: separating metadata (MongoDB) from binary artifacts (S3), precomputing search tokens at insert time, moving from regex to Lucene-backed Atlas Search, and routing reads/aggregations/analytics off the primary to secondaries and a hidden replica. The rest is standard Kubernetes HPA/KEDA and Cast AI node autoscaling.

takeaways.technique: Separate metadata store from artifact storage
takeaways.what_they_do: MongoDB holds only metadata (users, repos, config, billing, ACLs); model binaries/tokenizers live in S3, so metadata, storage, and compute scale independently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This separation of concern let us scale metadata independently from binary storage and compute independently from both.

takeaways.technique: Precompute at write time, not read time
takeaways.what_they_do: Model names are tokenized into a search-token array on insert, so queries hit a prebuilt index instead of doing regex scans at query time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We tokenize model names on insert time, not at query time.

takeaways.technique: Route heavy reads off the primary
takeaways.what_they_do: Only strongly-consistent writes and queries go to the primary; aggregations, change streams, and ad-hoc/reporting queries go to secondaries or a hidden replica isolated from production traffic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Primary should focus on what only primary can do. Anything else can be pushed to different machines.

takeaways.technique: Two-layer autoscaling on real workload metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: HPA scales pods on CPU/memory, Cast AI adds nodes when pods are pending, and they are moving to KEDA to scale on requests/sec and event-loop utilization instead of resource usage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: KDA scale on real application metrics like request per second or event loop utilization.

takeaways.technique: Index-backed search instead of regex scans
takeaways.what_they_do: Replaced MongoDB regex queries with Atlas Search (Lucene) autocomplete over precomputed tokens once regex latency broke at scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Reax doesn't scale well. So when our data set started to grow very quickly, we started to having problems with latency.
